title: Balkan kolo
summary: The kolo is the circle or chain dance of the Balkans: dancers hold hands or belts and move around together with small, quick steps while an accordion or a band keeps the pulse. Tunes run from the even two-beat narodno kolo to the limping seven-beat measures of the south-eastern Balkans.
howToPlay: Four pads are four foot actions: step with the right foot, step with the left, a hop, and a closing step that brings the feet together.
Marks fall toward the line; play the matching pad as each one lands, as the whole ring keeps the same step.
The two-beat tune is danced on the quarter note; the seven-beat tunes count seven short pulses in groups of three and two and two, or two and two and three.
rules: In the two-beat dance each beat is a quarter note and half-beat steps are the quick doubled steps.
In the seven-beat dances each pulse is one eighth note; steps fall on the first pulse of each group.
A step within a short moment of the mark is perfect; a close one is good; extra steps cost points.
Three stars need nearly every step on time.
heritageNote: Kolo, horo and oro are danced at weddings, fairs and village gatherings across the Balkans, and each region keeps its own tunes and step names. Every dancer keeps the same step, so a newcomer can join the line at any point.
credits: Dance: Balkan tradition; step patterns written for this game
